item.title: onot
item.description:
An open source notice file is a compliance artifact that provides users with copyright and license information for open source components included in supplied software. Writing notice files manually is error-prone and time-consuming. onot automates this process.

SK Telecom developed onot internally and released it as open source under the name onot. Kakao also contributed major features through collaborative development.

Features

onot takes an SBOM in SPDX format as input and automatically converts it into an open source notice file. It is Python-based, lightweight, and easy to use.

item.title: AI SBOM Compliance Guide
item.description:
This guide explains, one by one, each requirement of AI System Bill of Materials: Compliance Management Guide for the Supply Chain (Version 1.0), published by the OpenChain AI Work Group. It describes what verification materials each clause requires, how to comply, and what samples and tools can be used directly.

This specification carries the structure of the open source license compliance standard ISO/IEC 5230 (requirements, verification materials, rationale) over to the AI supply chain. It brings into the scope of compliance not only code but also the license and transparency obligations of model weights, training datasets, and the Model Tree.

item.title: Practical Guide to Open Source Management in the Financial Sector
item.description:
Financial institutions use more and more open source, yet they must manage it under conditions specific to their sector: closed networks, network separation regulations, supply chain security, and audit response. This guide connects the management procedures set out in the “Guide to Using and Managing Open Source Software in the Financial Sector” (금융분야 오픈소스 소프트웨어 활용·관리 안내서; Financial Supervisory Service (금융감독원) and Financial Security Institute (금융보안원), 2022) with the verification materials of the international standards ISO/IEC 5230 and 18974 and with the existing KWG practical guides. It shows practitioners, in an actionable form, what they need to put in place and in what order.

Author : OpenChain Korea Work Group / CC BY 4.0
